column1: subservient§Form should be subservient to the argument, not the other way round.§形式应**服从**论证，而不是反过来。
subsidize§Cheap fares are subsidized by everyone who never travels.§低票价是由从不出行的人共同**补贴**的。
subsist§Two species subsist on nothing but the bark of one tree.§有两个物种仅靠一种树的树皮**为生**。
subsistence§Subsistence farming leaves no record and feeds most of the world.§**自给**农业不留记录，却养活了世界大部分人口。
substance§Cross-examination showed the claim had no substance.§交叉盘问显示这项主张毫无**实质**。
substantial§A substantial breakfast is the whole strategy for a long walk.§一顿**丰盛**的早餐就是长途步行的全部策略。
substantiate§Substantiate the claim or withdraw it before the reprint.§要么**证实**这个说法，要么在重印前撤掉。
substantiation§Substantiation of the earlier date required two laboratories.§**证实**那个更早的年代需要两个实验室。
substantive§A substantive reply takes longer and settles more.§**实质性**的回复更费时，却能解决更多问题。
subtle§A subtle change of key carries the whole ending.§一次**微妙的**转调撑起了整个结尾。
subtract§Subtract the years he was ill and the output is astonishing.§**减去**他生病的那些年，产出量令人惊叹。
subversive§A subversive footnote is the safest place to say it.§脚注是说出**颠覆**性观点最安全的地方。
subvert§Good intentions can subvert a rule as thoroughly as bad ones.§好意可以像恶意一样彻底地**颠覆**一条规则。
successor§Naming a successor early cost him the last two years.§过早指定**继任者**让他失去了最后两年。
succinct§Be succinct in the abstract and generous in the notes.§摘要要**简洁**，注释要充分。
succulent§A succulent peach is worth the mess it makes.§一个**多汁的**桃子值得它弄出的狼藉。
succumb§He succumbed to the temptation to explain the joke.§他**没忍住**，还是解释了那个笑话。
sufficient§Sufficient unto the day is the paperwork thereof.§一天的文书工作，**够那一天**的了。
suffrage§Women's suffrage was won county by county, not all at once.§女性**选举权**是一个郡一个郡争来的，而非一蹴而就。
suggestive§A suggestive gap in the record is not the same as proof.§记录中一个**耐人寻味**的空白并不等于证据。
sundry§All and sundry were invited and about nine came.§**所有人**都受了邀请，来了大约九个。
supercede§The 1998 edition supercedes all earlier printings.§一九九八年版**取代**此前所有印次。
supercilious§A supercilious footnote is the worst kind.§**居高临下**的脚注是最糟糕的一种。
superficial§Superficial damage to the frame turned out to be structural.§画框**表面的**损伤后来发现是结构性的。
superficiality§Superficiality is often just a shortage of time.§**肤浅**往往只是时间不够。
superfluous§A superfluous adjective is the easiest thing to cut.§**多余的**形容词是最容易删掉的东西。
superiority§Assumed superiority is what makes a translation bad.§**自以为高明**，正是译文糟糕的原因。
superstitious§Sailors are superstitious about the same three things everywhere.§各地的水手都对同样的三件事**迷信**。
supplant§No format has yet supplanted the printed index card.§还没有哪种格式**取代**过印制的索引卡。
supple§A supple argument bends without breaking.§**柔韧**的论证能弯曲而不折断。
supplement§A dietary supplement is not a substitute for a meal.§膳食**补充**剂不能替代一顿饭。
supplementary§Supplementary questions revealed what the survey had missed.§**补充**提问揭示了调查遗漏的东西。
supplication§A letter of supplication survives from every year but one.§除了一年之外，每年都留下一封**陈情信**。
supportive§A supportive silence is sometimes the best response.§有时最好的回应是一种**支持**性的沉默。
suppress§Do not suppress an inconvenient result; explain it.§不要**压下**不利的结果，去解释它。
suppressive§Suppressive therapy reduces recurrence without curing anything.§**抑制**性治疗减少复发，却治不好病。
surfeit§A surfeit of choice at the beginning delays every project.§一开始**选择过多**会拖延每一个项目。
surly§The weather turned surly and the crossing was cancelled.§**天气转恶**，渡船取消了。
surmise§My surmise is that the second hand belongs to a clerk.§我**推测**第二种笔迹属于一位书吏。
surreptitious§A surreptitious glance at the answer helps nobody.§**偷看**答案对谁都没帮助。
surrogate§Attendance is a surrogate for interest and a poor one.§出勤率是兴趣的**替代指标**，而且很不好用。
susceptible§The argument is susceptible to one obvious objection.§这个论证**经不起**一个明显的反驳。
suspend§Dust suspended in the air makes the beam visible.§**悬浮**在空气中的尘埃让光束可见。
suspicion§A suspicion is not a finding, however often it is repeated.§**猜疑**不是结论，不管重复多少次。
suspicious§Be suspicious of a result that is exactly what you wanted.§对一个恰好符合你期待的结果要保持**怀疑**。
sustain§He sustained the note for an improbable length of time.§他把那个音**持续**了长得难以置信的时间。
sustenance§There is more sustenance in a footnote than in the preface.§一条脚注里的**养分**比序言还多。
sycophant§Surround yourself with sycophants and you will hear nothing useful.§身边围满**马屁精**，你就听不到任何有用的话。
syllogism§Not every argument is a syllogism, and that is a relief.§并非每个论证都是**三段论**，这倒是好事。
symbiotic§The lichen is symbiotic: an alga and a fungus living as one.§地衣是**共生**体：藻类与真菌合而为一。
symbolize§The colour symbolizes mourning in one country and marriage in another.§这种颜色在一个国家**象征**哀悼，在另一个国家象征婚姻。
symmetry§Perfect symmetry in a face reads as slightly wrong.§一张完全**对称**的脸看起来反而略显不对。
sympathetic§A sympathetic critic is not the same as a friendly one.§**体谅的**批评者与友善的批评者不是一回事。
symptomatic§The cough was symptomatic and the fever was not.§咳嗽是**症状**之一，发烧则不是。
syncopate§Syncopated rhythm puts the accent where the ear does not expect it.§**切分节奏**把重音放在耳朵意料之外的位置。
synergistic§A synergistic effect is claimed far more often than it is shown.§声称有**协同作用**的次数，远多于真正证明的次数。
synthesize§The body cannot synthesize this vitamin and must be given it.§人体无法**合成**这种维生素，必须从外界摄取。
tacit§Tacit knowledge is the reason apprenticeships still exist.§**默会知识**正是学徒制至今仍存在的原因。
taciturn§A taciturn colleague is not necessarily an unhappy one.§**沉默寡言的**同事未必不快乐。
tact§Tact is telling the truth in the order that can be heard.§**得体**，就是按对方听得进的顺序说真话。
tactful§A tactful silence is a skill nobody teaches.§**得体**的沉默是一门没人教的本事。
tactile§Tactile memory outlasts visual memory for tools.§对工具来说，**触觉**记忆比视觉记忆更持久。
tangential§Tangential reading is how most real discoveries begin.§大多数真正的发现都始于**离题**的阅读。
taunt§The taunt was recorded in the minutes and regretted at leisure.§那句**嘲讽**被记入了会议记录，事后慢慢后悔。
tawdry§Tawdry is what we call a taste we have grown out of.§我们把自己已经不再喜欢的品味称作**俗气**。
